summary.name: Ballpoint Pen Drawing, an explicitly named style in the Drawing and Illustration category. The source directly describes this visual direction.
summary.visualIdentity: Thin blue-black or black ballpoint lines use repeated contours and dense-to-sparse hatching on clean white or lightly warm paper. The look keeps a sketchbook character. Marks reveal in drawing order or as animated layered sketches. Heavy outlines and smooth vector fills are avoided.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit best-for examples are travel journals, field notes and idea-to-product stories. Sketchbook-style storytelling is the stated core use. Long narration holds and looping sketch backgrounds appear only as combination uses. Other uses, such as explanatory sketch sequences, are inferred from the visual cues.
summary.limitations: Hachure and pattern fills do not create authentic pen pressure, handwriting, paper texture or character poses. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical drawing production. Two-colour contrast checks do not cover text over textures or video. Heavy marker strokes, a second ink colour, smooth vector fills and boiling lettering are excluded. Live interaction is outside the video scope.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent, so the #FCFAF4 paper swatch is an illustrative suggestion, not a required canvas. Backgrounds may vary within clean white or lightly warm paper. Foreground #172C49 is a blue-black ink suggestion. Its contrast on the swatch is 13.477:1 for two colours only. Gradients are disabled, and tone comes from hatching. No exact approved colours are supplied, so task or brand colours would override these values.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Marks should reveal in a plausible pen order, and line boil must not occur while lines are still drawing. Movement should be smooth and authored, while sharp cuts and reading holds stay deliberate. Optional references are motion-012, a progress-linked chapter handoff, and motion-015, synchronized story steps. Both are optional and need scene compatibility. Interactive delivery may use tap or focus reveals, with static states under reduced motion.
summary.audio: No specific audio is specified, and the metadata gives no fixed genre, tempo, voice or mandatory layer. Options include music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience or silence, chosen by topic. Narration and reading holds take priority over music. Silence is valid. Motion references need no attached sound, and no audio assets are supplied.
summary.assetRequirements: No mandatory uploads are specified. Contours and hatching are stored as SVG paths, and fine pen texture is composited in Canvas. Exact copy, local fonts and any approved colour values must be supplied when they apply. Subject, audience, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate and output directory are unspecified template placeholders. Optional sketch geometry may be generated locally.
summary.combinations: Style-024, margin notes, adds same-pen arrows and handwritten labels for explanatory pages. Notes must use the same single ink and appear only after the referenced drawing completes. Style-092, hold treatment, adds subtle boil between two pen variants for long narration. Variants differ only in hatch placement, at one fixed slow cadence. Support styles should be added only when they fit these rules.
summary.productionApproach: The style renderer is SVG for contours and hatching, Canvas 2D for pen texture and seeded Rough.js geometry only where sketch-like marks are called for. The motion engine is GSAP, with Motion optional and explicitly synchronized. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition, checks, snapshots and export. Remotion is only a fallback when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation applies. Chroma-js validates colours and contrast. Randomness must be seeded and shapes cached.
